- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for high-impact days.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” adjustment: subtract 1–3% from forecast for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: over-predicts downward trends after prolonged upward moves; adjust forecast by adding 1–3% to counteract overcorrection.
- Forecast horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts often overestimate by 2–8% in the first 5–7 days; apply a “decay factor” to reduce forecast magnitude early in the horizon.
- Model underestimates late-period volatility; increase forecast by 1–3% for days 25–30 if true outcome shows >10% deviation from mean or recent trend.
